$comment: APPROVED, NAMED, EXPIRING suppressions for the integration shard.
A test that appears here is still counted against the full EXPECTED population. It is not removed
from the denominator, because reducing the denominator by the tests you expect to skip encodes the
suppression into the success criterion: the gate then passes forever while those tests never run.
Every suppression this project has found was justified when it was written, and every one survived
for the same structural reason -- doing nothing preserved it. So neglect must REMOVE a suppression,
* expires, id and owner are MANDATORY. An entry missing any of them fails the gate, so the
* a PAST expiry is a REFUSE, not a warning. The suppression stops working and the build stops.
* renewal requires FRESH EVIDENCE, not a fresh date. Bumping the date is the failure mode that
would defeat the whole mechanism, because it makes an unreviewed entry LOOK reviewed. Record a
new measurement in evidence: what was run, on what, and what it showed.
* the list may only SHRINK. Growth is a reviewable diff with a named approver, never a runtime
The gate prints this file in full on every run, with days remaining. Suppressions become invisible

REFERENCE DIRECTION. This file is mirrored and world-visible, so it carries NO internal tracker id. The tracking issue names this entry by its 'id'; this entry never names the issue. Internal artifacts may point at public ones, never the reverse -- a public file that cites an internal work item leaks it and means nothing to the consumer reading it.

entries.reason: The class self-skips on any Linux CI runner (Assert.SkipWhen on isLinuxRunner && isCi). The guard's stated justification is 'unstable on Linux CI runners'.
entries.evidence: NOT YET MEASURED ON THE PLATFORM IT GUARDS. Every observation held is from a Windows developer box (RUNNER_OS unset, CI unset); the suite passes there 14/14 in 68-294ms. The instability claim has never been reproduced on a Linux CI runner, so this entry records an UNVERIFIED premise, deliberately, rather than presenting it as established.

entries.reason: All 15 facts call SkipIfVaultUnavailable(), which is Assert.SkipWhen(_provider is null, "AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI environment variable not set"). The variable is never set in CI, so the provider is always null and every fact skips. Unlike Cosmos DB there is no Azure Key Vault emulator, so this cannot be closed by adding a container: it needs a real Key Vault resource and credentials in the CI environment.
entries.evidence: Measured 2026-08-01 on the committed tree. The class declares 15 [Fact] and 0 [Theory]; all 15 route through SkipIfVaultUnavailable() at AzureKeyVaultProviderIntegrationShould.cs:332. AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI appears exactly once in the workflow tree, at ci.yml:655, inside a step whose own comment reads 'These are DIAGNOSTIC PRINTS, not probes... they cannot fail' -- it reports whether the variable is set and never sets it. No workflow assigns it and no secret is bound to it. So the skip is not intermittent and not environmental drift: it is the guaranteed outcome of every run on the current configuration, and has been for as long as the variable has been unset. What is NOT established: whether these 15 facts pass against a real Key Vault. They have not been observed running anywhere, so this entry records untested coverage, not passing coverage.
